body: Envelope::check silently passes NaN values in all f64 fields (pH, DO, TAN, NO2, NO3, reproductive_readiness, plant_biomass, algae_nuisance, biofilter_maturity, periphyton_biomass, fast_stem_biomass) because NaN comparisons return false in IEEE 754. Add a NaN/Inf guard at the top of the check method: for every constrained f64 field, if the snapshot value is not finite, push a violation like 'pH is NaN (expected [{min}, {max}])'. The existing final_finite assertions only catch NaN at the end of multi-hour runs, not at intermediate checkpoints where the root cause would be easier to diagnose.
